stumbles.quote: Jev will not review declaude_lint's hits before a post goes out.
stumbles.why: Opening claim is unexplained: declaude_lint is never defined, and it's unclear whether Jev is barred from the review or from a narrower task. The title says it "settles a quarter of the lint's hits" while this says it won't review them.

stumbles.quote: Jev settles a quarter of the lint's hits and stays out of the review
stumbles.why: "Settles" is undefined here. It only becomes clear later that it means the hits Jev could decide within the 5% error budget. The section also never says whether "the review" is the same thing as the lint.

stumbles.quote: Jev is a small decision model that returns a calibrated probability for a yes/no question in about 160 ms.
stumbles.why: The text doesn't say what Jev is, who made it, or what yes/no question it was asked about each hit. "Routing questions" in the next sentence is also unexplained.
register.md and the meaning of "tic" are never explained. The reader can't tell what a tic is or what the definition contains.

stumbles.quote: A baseline that knows only the hit's lint category, which gives it the category's historical tic rate, reached 0.769.
stumbles.why: The text doesn't explain where the historical rates come from. They might be computed on the same 261 hits, which would leak the labels. It's also unclear why a 0.769 baseline is described as beating Jev's 0.808.

stumbles.quote: At a 5% error budget it could settle only 24.5% of hits.
stumbles.why: It isn't explained what "settle" or "error budget" means mechanically. It's also unclear which set of hits the percentage is measured over: the 300 or the 261.

stumbles.quote: The bar set in advance was 50%.
stumbles.why: The text doesn't say who set the bar or why it's 50%. It also doesn't say whether the 50% bar was a requirement for adding Jev to the review.

stumbles.quote: Triad hits were real tics in 5 of 44 cases, participle hits in 5 of 43, and negation-first hits in 16 of 18.
stumbles.why: Triad, participle and negation-first are undefined lint categories. The counts total 105 hits, so the reader can't tell whether they are drawn from the 261 or from the 300.

point: Jev, a small probability model, ranked lint hits only modestly better than a category-rate baseline and settled just 24.5% of hits at a 5% error budget, below the 50% bar, so it was not added to the review.
